'''Engler''': {{legend0|#e27f7f|50–60%}} {{legend0|#d75d5d|60–70%}} {{legend0|#d72f30|70–80%}} {{legend0|#c21b18|80–90%}}
'''Fieger''': {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = [[Governor of Michigan|Governor]] | before_election = [[John Engler]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[John Engler]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) }} {{ElectionsMI}} The '''1998 Michigan gubernatorial election''' was held on November 3, 1998, to elect the [[Governor of Michigan|governor]] and [[Lieutenant Governor of Michigan|lieutenant governor]] of [[Michigan]]. Republican incumbent [[John Engler]] was re-elected to a third term in office over [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] lawyer [[Geoffrey Fieger]] in a landslide.{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1998/11/05/us/the-1998-elections-state-by-state-midwest-michigan.html|title=The 1998 elections: state by state -- Midwest; Michigan|date=November 5, 1998|access-date=July 31, 2011|work=[[The New York Times]]|first=Matthew L.|last=Wald}} Engler won the Republican nomination against token opposition. Fieger, who was best known for representing the [[assisted suicide]] advocate [[Jack Kevorkian]], funded his own successful campaign for the Democratic nomination and defeated East Lansing mayor Larry Owen and former state senator Doug Ross. As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this was the last time [[Genesee County, Michigan|Genesee County]] and [[Washtenaw County, Michigan|Washtenaw County]] voted for the Republican gubernatorial candidate. == Background == Although Michigan voters had passed a ballot measure in 1992 limiting governors to two terms in office, it was not retroactive and counted only towards people taking office in or after 1993.{{Cite web |title=Michigan Ballot Proposal B, Term Limits for Congressional, State Executive, and State Legislative Offices Initiative (1992) |url=https://ballotpedia.org/Michigan_Ballot_Proposal_B,_Term_Limits_for_Congressional,_State_Executive,_and_State_Legislative_Offices_Initiative_(1992) |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=Ballotpedia |language=en}}{{Cite web |title=MCL - Article V § 30 - Michigan Legislature |url=https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=MCL-ARTICLE-V-30 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250523013421/https://www.legislature.mi.gov/Laws/MCL?objectName=MCL-ARTICLE-V-30 |archive-date=2025-05-23 |access-date=2025-07-27 |website=www.legislature.mi.gov |language=en}} As Engler had first taken office in 1991, his first term did not count towards the two-term limit, and he was allowed to run for a third term. ==Republican primary== ===Candidates=== * Gary Artinian * [[John Engler]], incumbent [[governor of Michigan]] since 1991 ===Campaign=== Engler, a two-term incumbent, faced token opposition in the Republican primary, winning re-nomination with almost 90 percent of the vote. Following [[Lieutenant Governor of Michigan|lieutenant governor]] [[Connie Binsfeld]]'s decision to not seek a third term, [[Michigan Senate|Michigan Senate majority leader]] [[Dick Posthumus]] received the Republican nomination for lieutenant governor.{{cite web |url=http://www.crainsdetroit.com/article/19981019/SUB/810190856/decision-98-a-look-at-key-elections |title=DECISION '98: A LOOK AT KEY ELECTIONS |work=Crains Detroit |date=October 16, 1998 |access-date=October 12, 2017}} ===Results=== [[File:1998 Michigan gubernatorial Republican primary election results map by county.svg|thumb|260px|Results by county {{collapsible list | title = {{legend|#ed8783|Engler}} |{{legend|#d02923|70–80%}} |{{legend|#b00600|80–90%}} |{{legend|#850400|>90%}} }} |center]] {{Election box begin no change |title=Republican primary results{{cite web |title=1998 Michigan Election Results - 8/4/1998 State Primary |url=https://mvic.sos.state.mi.us/votehistory/Index?type=C&electionDate=8-4-1998 |publisher=Michigan Department of State |access-date=14 June 2026}} }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party = Republican Party (United States) |candidate = [[John Engler]] ([[Incumbent|inc.]]) |votes = 477,628 |percentage = 89.60% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change| |party = Republican Party (United States) |candidate = Gary Artinian |votes = 55,453 |percentage = 10.40% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 533,081 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== * [[Geoffrey Fieger]], attorney known for representing [[Jack Kevorkian]] * Larry Owen, former mayor of [[East Lansing, Michigan|East Lansing]] * Doug Ross, former state senator from [[Oak Park, Michigan|Oak Park]] ===Candidates=== Early in the race, Owen was considered the front runner.{{cite web |url=http://www.ourcampaigns.com/CandidateDetail.html?CandidateID=24243 |title=Larry Owen |work=Our Campaigns |date=March 16, 2013 |access-date=October 12, 2017}} But due to Fieger's notoriety and personal wealth, he surpassed his opponents. He ended up spending almost $6 million of his own money in the race.{{cite web |url=http://www.freep.com/story/news/2017/05/12/geoffrey-fieger-michigan-governor/319594001/ |title=Geoffrey Fieger considering a return to politics with run for governor |author=Kathleen Gray |work=Detroit Free Press |date=May 12, 2017 |access-date=October 12, 2017}} Fieger won a close race, taking 41 percent of the vote.{{cite web |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-1998-aug-06-mn-10629-story.html |title=Kevorkian's Lawyer Wins Gubernatorial Primary in Michigan |work=Los Angeles Times |date=August 6, 1998 |access-date=October 12, 2017 |author=Associated Press}} State representative Jim Agee, after securing the support from the [[Michigan Education Association]] was picked by Fieger to be his running mate, over Fieger's initial preferred choice, state representative [[Candace A. Curtis|Candace Curtis]].{{cite web |url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/1998/08/29/teachers-pleased-by-fieger-running-mate/ |title=Teachers Pleased By Fieger Running Mate |date=August 29, 1998|access-date=October 12, 2017 |work=Chicago Tribune |author=}} ===Results=== [[File:1998 Michigan gubernatorial Democratic primary election results map by county.svg|thumb|260px|Results by county {{collapsible list | title = {{legend|#8da9e2|Fieger}} |{{legend|#dee8fb|30–40%}} |{{legend|#b4c7ec|40–50%}} |{{legend|#8da9e2|50–60%}} }} {{collapsible list | title = {{legend|#73bc84|Owen}} |{{legend|#d6efdc|30–40%}} |{{legend|#a3d5af|40–50%}} |{{legend|#73bc84|50–60%}} |{{legend|#3fa457|60–70%}} }} {{collapsible list | title = {{legend|#c88fe4|Ross}} |{{legend|#f2dffc|30–40%}} }} |center]] {{Election box begin no change | title=Democratic primary results }} {{Election box winning candidate with party link no change |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = [[Geoffrey Fieger]] |votes = 300,458 |percentage = 41.18% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change| |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = Larry Owen |votes = 272,360 |percentage = 37.33% }} {{Election box candidate with party link no change| |party = Democratic Party (United States) |candidate = Doug Ross |votes = 156,847 |percentage = 21.50% }} {{Election box total no change | votes = 729,665 | percentage = 100.00% }} {{Election box end}} ==General election== === Candidates === * [[John Engler]], incumbent [[governor of Michigan]] since 1991 (Republican) * [[Geoffrey Fieger]], attorney known for representing [[Jack Kevorkian]] (Democratic) ===Polling=== {| class="wikitable" style="font-size:90%;text-align:center;" |- valign=bottom !
